messages.author: 722521532a54784f
messages.subject: Unclear "Overall Missing rate" - in gel.report.callrate
parts:
Hi everyone, 
this is probably a silly question, but I am a bit confused on what the "missing rate" value provided with "gl.report.callrate" means.

I have filtered 1st for individual CR with a 0.50 threshold, and then with 2 different Locus CR thresholds of 0.60 or 0.99.
I then checked again the Individual CR after filtering for Locus CR, and I get the following:
- dataset filtered with Locus CR 0.60 --> Ind CR "Missing rate overall" = 0.07
- dataset filtered with Locus CR 0.99 --> Ind CR  "Missing rate overall" = 0

However, in gboth datasets, ther are individuals which don't have all the loci. So, for example in the dataset filtered for Locus CR 0.99, 21 individuals are removed with a Ind CR 0.99 applied after the Locus CR filter.
So, what does the "Overall missing rate" mean and why it is "0" here if some individuals are still missing data related to some loci?

I would appreciate some clarifications.
Thanks a lot as usual!
Best,
Gabriella

messages.author: 9e12eec50c435b60
messages.subject: Re: [dartR] Unclear "Overall Missing rate" - in gel.report.callrate
parts:
Hi Gabrielle,

One of the difficulties with filtering on call rate is that you may have 20% missing data based on the total number of loci as the denominator, then you take 10% of them out by filtering, and find that you don't have 10% left. This is because the denominator on the percentage estimate changes when you delete loci during filtering. If you want 10% left at the end of the filtering (as opposed to deleting 10% of what you start with), you need to reapply the filter repeatedly until the end value stabilizes.

I suspect that is what is going on anyway.

Arthur

messages.author: 592079bda2cb3220
messages.subject: Re: [dartR] Unclear "Overall Missing rate" - in gel.report.callrate
parts:
Hi Gabriella,

I think the problems is that the value reported in  “Missing Rate Overall” is rounded to two decimals. To fix this, I changed it to report four decimals.

You can use this updated function by installing the developing version of dartR by typing in the R console in RStudio:

> library(dartR)
> gl.install.vanilla.dartR(flavour = "dev")

Please let me know if that makes sense.

Regards,
Luis
